Question B-003-018-008.

Why the correct answer is right: The safe priority is to de-energize the source, summon emergency help, and give first aid only when it is safe; touching the victim while energized can make the rescuer part of the circuit.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Wait for a few minutes to see if the person can get away from the high voltage on their own, then try to help": Waiting allows burning or shock to continue; the urgent action is to remove power safely and call for help.
- sourceIndex 2: "Immediately drag the person away from the high voltage": Directly grabbing the person can put the rescuer in the current path, creating a second casualty.
- sourceIndex 3: "Run from the area so you won't be burned too": Moving to safety may be necessary briefly, but simply running away ignores de-energizing, emergency calling, and first aid when safe.
